svg.title: One lookup column, three names in the Web API
svg.desc: The Site lookup on the Work order table appears under three different names depending on what you do. Reading the ID: the lookup value property _cedar_site_value, lower case with underscores, returns the GUID of the related site and is used in $select and $filter. Reading the related row: the single-valued navigation property cedar_Site, which uses the schema name with its capital letter, is used in $expand and in filters across the relationship such as cedar_Site/cedar_sitecode eq 'HV-B'. Writing the lookup: the navigation property with the suffix @odata.bind, cedar_Site@odata.bind, set to the path /cedar_sites(guid), is used in POST and PATCH bodies. Using the logical name cedar_site in any of the three places fails. A fourth box shows the opposite direction: the collection-valued navigation property on Site that returns its work orders, whose name is the relationship schema name found in the $metadata document.
svg.text: Work order → Site: the same lookup has three names
Schema name: mind the capital S.
Value is a path, not a bare GUID.
Use in POST and PATCH bodies:
What fails, and the other direction
The logical name cedar_site works in none of the three places: "Could not find a property named 'cedar_site'" or "undeclared property".
Site → its work orders is a collection-valued navigation property named after the relationship; look it up in $metadata, do not guess.
